subject: prediction of expected abundance in ZIP-N-mixture model

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: prediction of expected abundance in ZIP-N-mixture model
parts:
Dear all,

I've been running N-mix model analyses for some Swiss songbirds and compared all three mixture distributions available in pcount() in terms of AIC and GOF (the latter by parametric bootstrap). The ZIP mixture models fit best overall and so I want to use them to predict expected abundance in relation to the modelled environmental covariates and also map those predictions for all of Switzerland (i.e., produce a species distribution map).

Now my question is this: how do I have to incorporate the zero-inflation parameter into these predictions if I compute them "by hand" ? Is the following correct ?

pred.lambda <- (1 - theta) * exp(linear predictor)  

where "theta" is the zero-inflation parameter and "linear predictor" is the linear model for log(lambda) ?

And If I use predict(), then I currently only get the point estimate, but not the SE nor CIs, right ?

Thanks for comments.

Kind regards  --  Marc
